messages:
jordan: heads-up — prod gpu pool in us-west hit a sudden memory spike around 22:03 UTC, multiple requests OOM'd; logs show allocator failures and kvcache thrash. Anyone oncall?
kai: i'm here. saw the alert, looking at live profiles now. seems related to large n=1 requests with 16k context + long beams causing workspace blowout.
maya: can you paste the profiler snippet? curious if kernel selector switched to fallback kernels causing bigger temporary buffers.
jordan: paste below. not the prettiest but shows the inflection.
```
[profile] request_id=abc123
kernel: fused_attention_v2 -> switched at step 12
workspace_peak: 11.7 GB
kv_cache_allocated: 6.1 GB
allocator_failures: 3
backtrace: runtime::alloc::gpu::reserve -> kvcache::reserve -> request_shaper
```
kai: yep kernel switch at step 12 is suspicious — that usually happens when sequence len changes mid-request or when compiled kernels don't support the current seq distribution.
maya: quick mitigation candidates: 1) enable request-level headroom (reduce workspace target by 20%), 2) force earlier fallback to quantized LLM variant, 3) circuit-breaker drop for requests over 12k tokens.
samir: I can push a hotfix route to force model-variant=quant-8 for the affected deployment. that should cut workspace ~35% and reduce kv cache pressure.
jordan: for immediate triage, please do both: samir flip the route, kai apply the headroom change to runtime configs. we need to avoid rolling restarts.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: started rollout of route override to service=embedder-prod, variant=quant-8 — uid rollout-2234567001
kai: applied headroom tweak: set runtime.workspace_headroom_ratio=0.8 for pool gpu-us-west-3. Also enabled short-circuit caching on prefix matches.
maya: also bump circuit breaker threshold: in-flight tokens cap -> 48k -> 32k for that pool, and enable request-shape trimming for >14k token inputs.
jordan: results so far: error rate dropped from 6.8% -> 0.9% within 30s. latency stable.
```
metrics before/after:
err_rate: 0.068 -> 0.009
p95 latency: 280ms -> 310ms (+diff due to quant fallback)
avg memory usage pool: 73% -> 48%
```
samir: good. i'll keep route override for 2 hours, then we'll canary a staged rollback to the float model but with persistent headroom and trimming.
kai: follow-up action items:
- add a kernel-selector gate: don't switch to fused_attention_v2 if peak workspace > 10GB predicted for the request (assign: kai)
- refine batching heuristic to fuse only if seq_stddev < 400 and avg_len < 4k (assign: jordan)
- add a telemetry counter for mid-request kernel switches (assign: maya)
- create an automated fallback playbook that toggles quantized variant + headroom when kv_pressure > 0.7 (assign: samir)
maya: I'll draft the playbook snippet. quick sketch:
```
if kv_cache_hit_rate < 0.2 and kv_cache_alloc/util > 0.7:
  set model_variant=quant-8
  set workspace_headroom_ratio=0.75
  enable request_trim(max_tokens=14000)
  notify @oncall
```
jordan: thanks all. can someone file a postmortem with root cause hypothesis and timeline? i'll start the doc and add telemetry graphs.
ops-bot: incident-bot: incident 2234567001 acked by samir. tags: oom, headroom, kvcache, kernel-switch
kai: leaving a note: the kernel selector change is low-risk but should have unit tests — i'll open a PR and add perf tests on the seq-dist harness.
maya: i'll own the telemetry counter + playbook PR.
samir: i'll keep the route override until noon PST, then coordinate the canary with load at 15%.
jordan: great. wrap up in #eng-runtime postmortems once PM review. :thumbsup!
